codex.section: Recommended exact spec diff — §12.3 resource values and optional estimate

steps.claim: Target cost expressions admit division, and §8.2 aggregates their exact rational values. The resource schema stores decimal values; §10.1 supplies upward decimal encoding and exact-resource binding for estimates.

The proposed rule requires exact resource accounting for every context, leaves estimate optional, and invokes §10.1 encodings only for an estimate in the record. It supplies no numeric encoding or comparison default for a non-estimate report with a non-terminating resource value.

Change the witness target’s native duration to {"op":"/","args":[1,3]} and omit estimate. Each child’s exact time is 1/3; the root time is 2/3. Neither has a finite exact decimal representation. Reproduction: python3 -I -B -c 'from fractions import Fraction as F; print(F(1,3), 2*F(1,3))'.

A checker comparing the reported decimal to the exact rational rejects every possible time value, while one extending K12’s rounding convention accepts its upward encoding. The amended text must select that verdict; this is not merely an unspecified serialization layout.

codex.fix: In §12.3 add: 'For every resources map, including single-context maps, resource_contexts records and unkeyed projections, accounting is performed in exact rational arithmetic. Whether or not estimate is present, each reported value uses §10.1’s canonical 34-significant-digit upward decimal encoding. The checker compares that encoding with the encoding of its recomputed exact value, not the displayed decimal with the exact rational. When estimate is present, its reduced exact_resources fractions MUST also equal the recomputed values; K12’s existing mandatory-estimate obligations remain unchanged.' Thus time 1/3 displays as '0.3333333333333333333333333333333334'; an included exact_resources entry is {"numerator":"1","denominator":"3"}. A viable alternative is to require estimate whenever any total lacks an exact finite decimal representation, retaining exact decimal equality otherwise. I recommend the unconditional encoding rule.
